lesson.grammar_point: modals of permission and obligation (can / can't / have to)

listenings.text: Right, quick tour and then I will leave you alone. Kitchen is open all day, so help yourself, you don't have to ask. There are bikes in the garage and you can take one whenever you want. Two things you have to do: the bins go out on Tuesday night, and you do your own laundry on Sunday. That is it, that is the whole list. You don't have to cook, we do that, although you can help if you feel like it. One thing you can't do: never leave the back door open, because the dog gets out and then we spend the evening looking for him. Your spare key is on the hook by the door.

Okay, so that was the official version. Here is the real one. The curfew on school nights is real, do not test it. But at the weekend nobody actually cares, as long as you send a message. The one rule you should never break is the bins. If you forget the bins, everybody is angry for a week and you will hear about it every single day. Also, mum says you don't have to cook, and that is true, but if you cook once she will talk about it for a month. Oh, and I have an old board in the shed. You can share it until your boards arrive.

reading.rtitle: Welcome, Renato -- a few things about the house
paras: The kitchen is open all day, so help yourself. You don't have to ask, and you don't have to wait for us. There is always fruit on the table and there is always bread.

Two things are obligatory. You have to put the bins out on Tuesday night, and you have to do your own laundry on Sunday. That is the whole list of chores, and everybody in this house has the same kind of list.

On school nights you have to be home by nine thirty. At the weekend you can stay out later, but you have to send a message first. Your spare key is on the hook by the door, so you can come in late without waking anybody up.
You don't have to cook. We cook, and you are very welcome to help if you want to. You can use the bikes in the garage at any time, and you can share the surfboards in the shed with Jack.
One thing you can't do: leave the back door open. The dog gets out, and then we all spend the evening looking for him. And the last person out of the house always has to lock up.
